subject: TLS edge role matrix and DNS ownership — Acme private endpoints
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme-payments.com>, security@acme-payments.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: TLS edge role matrix and DNS ownership — Acme private endpoints

Hi Alice / Acme Sec team,

Following our runbook review last week, attached is a concise ops plan that lays out ownership for TLS termination and DNS for the private VPC endpoints Redwood will expose during the Proof-of-Concept. The spreadsheet contains a role matrix (who controls cert issuance, renewal windows, rotation order, and where TLS is terminated), as well as recommended guardrails for mutual-TLS vs. TLS passthrough choices.

Key asks for this thread:
- Confirm Acme’s preference for certificate issuer: customer-managed (Acme PKI/HSM) or Redwood-managed (Redwood CA + customer roots).
- Confirm whether Acme will own the FQDN delegation for the internal hostnames (e.g., private-api.acme-payments.internal) or prefer Redwood to host under a delegated subdomain.
- Any constraints around egress inspection or forced TLS termination inside your VPC we should be aware of.

We’ve included two high-level options in the matrix:
1) Customer-owned certs + split-DNS: Acme issues certs and controls DNS for private FQDNs — Redwood terminates TLS at the private load balancer but uses customer certs. Good for security/regulatory audits.
2) Redwood-managed certs + delegated DNS records: Redwood manages issuance and renewal, Acme delegates DNS zone or specific records. Simpler for operations; requires DNS delegation agreement.

Attached: tls-edge-role-matrix.xlsx (role matrix), dns-ownership-draft.md (proposal text), acme-tls-checklist.pdf (audit checklist).

If you want, we can run a short 30-minute technical huddle to walk the matrix and lock decisions. Proposed times: Monday 10am PT or Tuesday 2pm PT.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure Products
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TLS edge role matrix and DNS ownership — Acme private endpoints

Jonas, thanks for the clear summary and the attachments — skimmed the matrix and looks thorough. A few clarifications from our side before we pick a lane: 

- Preference: security would prefer customer-managed certs where possible, but we're open to Redwood-managed if we retain audit logs and the private CA root is under our control (exportable proof). We cannot put private keys into Redwood-managed HSMs.
- DNS: we prefer to keep zone authority inside our accounts for compliance reasons. That said, we can delegate a narrow subdomain (e.g., redwood-acme.svc.internal) if that's necessary and can be revoked programmatically.
- MTLS: We need mTLS for all control-plane RPCs; data-plane ingress can be TLS with client cert validation for higher-tier flows.

Can Marissa / Karthik confirm whether the Redwood private load balancer can accept customer-supplied cert bundles and whether your rotation workflow supports overlapping certs (for zero-downtime swap)? Also: is there an API for Acme to trigger immediate rotation in an emergency?

Best,
Alice Turner
Head of Platform Security
Acme Payments
alice.turner@acme-payments.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme-payments.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TLS edge role matrix and DNS ownership — Acme private endpoints

Hi Alice — quick technical answers to your questions: 

- Customer cert support: yes. Our private LB accepts PEM bundles (chain + cert + intermediates). Private keys must stay in your HSM but we support either:
  * Bring-your-own-key via ACME over a customer-managed CA (you issue certs and upload the PEM chain), or
  * Bring-your-own-KMS: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) to call-sign CSRs; private key never leaves your HSM.

- Rotation and overlap: our endpoint plane supports parallel cert slots and staged activation. Typical flow: upload new cert chain -> verify -> stage on second slot -> flip traffic -> retire old. We also provide an API to trigger immediate activation; rotate events are logged in the audit stream and surface to your SIEM via our secure webhook.

- mTLS: supported at the application listener level for mutually authenticated RPCs. We can provide a short demo of mTLS handshake logs so you can see certificate fingerprinting and expiry telemetry.

- Emergency rotation API: yes — documented in the attached dns-ownership-draft.md under section 3.2, and we’ll add an explicit example script for Acme’s team (we’ll push a gist after this thread).

I'll schedule the 30-minute huddle for Monday 10am PT unless you prefer the alternate. Let us know.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Turner <alice.turner@acme-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TLS edge role matrix and DNS ownership — Acme private endpoints

Thanks Alice — appreciate the constraints. A couple of operational commitments from Redwood to make this workable: 

- We'll implement the delegated subdomain model you suggested: Acme creates redwood-acme.svc.internal NS records and delegates that narrow zone to Redwood nameservers. This gives Acme revocation control while letting Redwood automate certificate lifecycles.

- For auditability: we will ship a daily signed export of certificate events (issued, rotated, revoked) to the S3 bucket you control; entries will include cert serial, fingerprint, issuer, subject, and timestamp.

- Emergency rotation: we will provide an Ops API token scoped to certificate actions (rotate/revoke) and an example runbook. Tokens will be short-lived and require multi-signer approval for production scopes.

Next steps:
1) Alice / Acme to confirm delegation capability and provide the zone name and expected TTLs.
2) Jonas/Marissa to send the staged activation demo and the emergency rotation script gist.
3) Agree on rotation windows (we propose 48-hour overlap for major certs and 24-hour for leaf certs).

I'll follow up with the demo link and the initial Ops API docs by COB Monday.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Inference Serving
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
